name: ripgrep
summary: A Rust line-oriented recursive search tool that combines ignore-aware parallel traversal, configurable regex engines, adaptive file searching, and structured streaming output.

features.name: Ignore-aware parallel traversal
features.description: The official README documents a lock-free parallel recursive directory iterator and default filtering of VCS-ignored, hidden, and binary files. The fixed repository contains the ignore and search crates that implement this traversal boundary.
benefits: Reduces unnecessary filesystem work for source-tree searches
Uses parallel directory traversal while retaining configurable ignore semantics
costs: Results and errors arrive from concurrent traversal work
Ignore configuration can make an apparently complete search intentionally incomplete

features.name: Regex search-engine pipeline
features.description: ripgrep separates matcher, regex, searcher, printer, and CLI crates. The default regex path uses Rust's finite-automata-oriented engine with Unicode support, while PCRE2 is an explicit optional or automatic-hybrid choice.
benefits: Allows matching, file searching, and result rendering to evolve behind crate boundaries
Combines Unicode-aware matching with literal and automata optimizations
costs: Regex features and performance depend on the selected engine and pattern
A richer pipeline increases configuration and semantic compatibility surface

features.name: Adaptive file search and streaming output
features.description: The official README describes choosing memory maps or incremental buffered searching according to workload, and the source exposes searcher and printer components for line-oriented result delivery. Structured output modes provide a machine-readable boundary.
benefits: Adapts file reading strategy to single-file and large-directory workloads
Supports both human-readable and downstream-processable result streams
costs: Output ordering, buffering, and backpressure affect observable behavior
Binary, encoding, and multiline modes add distinct processing paths

mathematical_views.question: How do roots, ignore rules, file-type filters, workers, and matching tasks determine the set of searched files?
assumptions: Traversal produces a stream of candidate paths and filters are predicates over paths and metadata
Parallel workers may reorder internal processing while preserving the output contract selected by the CLI
The view abstracts filesystem races, permission errors, and exact work-stealing behavior

mathematical_views.question: How does a pattern become matches, context records, and serialized output across regex, searcher, and printer stages?
assumptions: Each stage is modeled as a transformation over bytes, lines, matches, or result records
The selected regex engine defines the matcher relation for the invocation
The view abstracts terminal coloring, buffering details, and platform-specific file access

benefits: Concurrent search avoids irrelevant paths by default
costs: Filtering policy and concurrent delivery complicate completeness and ordering

benefits: Composable engines and stages support fast Unicode search
costs: Engine choice and pattern shape affect semantics and performance

benefits: I/O strategy and output form fit interactive or pipeline use
costs: Buffering, encoding, and output mode choices increase behavior surface
